A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPD-Sheaf research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original MoleculeNet experiments, architectural ablations, depth and effective-rank analyses, EEG classification, and ZINC regression.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds molecular scaling experiments, oversmoothing diagnostics, graph perturbation experiments, and additional EEG comparisons.

M1.justification: The core architecture, update equations, and implementation remain unchanged. However, new Appendix G describes a GCN semantic stream, whereas Section 5.1 and Appendix D specify GraphSAGE, while claiming no architectural modification. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is a wording error or an actual experimental variant.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on the approximately 437,000-molecule ogbg-molpcba dataset, representation-collapse tests on Cora and Texas, and edge-deletion and rewiring scenarios on BACE and BBBP. This substantially extends the evaluated data and input conditions. EEG and ZINC coverage already existed in v1.

E2.justification: EEG Table 6 expands from three comparators to six by adding TSMNet, GyroAtt, and Graph-CSPNet. Appendix E.5 identifies TSMNet and GyroAtt as rerun comparisons and Graph-CSPNet scores as quoted results. These stronger comparators materially change the EEG rankings; the existing MoleculeNet and ZINC comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include the official OGB scaffold split with Average Precision, Dirichlet-energy and MAD measurements at depths 2–128, and ROC-AUC retention under edge deletion or rewiring at rates 0.1, 0.3, and 0.5. These extend the evaluation design; the previously documented MoleculeNet, EEG, and ZINC protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds direct representation-collapse diagnostics across molecular, homophilic, and heterophilic graphs, supplementing the retained depth-performance plot. Appendix I adds controlled perturbation experiments testing whether SPD stalks increase dependence on edge structure. These address substantive additional diagnostic and mechanistic questions.

E5.justification: Table 6 changes from uniformly reporting mean and standard deviation to explicitly reporting deviations only where available; the three added EEG comparators have point estimates only. Existing five-run MoleculeNet and four-run ZINC reporting is unchanged. No increased run counts or new statistical tests are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 9–11 add substantial results, including ogbg-molpcba AP of 0.2419 versus GCN's 0.2020 and BACE retention under 50% edge deletion of 69.5% versus Euclidean SheafNN's 83.0%. Existing EEG scores remain 83.25%, 85.58%, and 82.58%, but now rank second, third, and first. Existing MoleculeNet and ZINC numerical results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 7.1 adds an equivariance condition for restriction maps and a candidate construction using SPD eigenvectors and an invariantly predicted orthogonal matrix. This is a limited mathematical extension presented as future work. The existing definitions, theorems, appendix proofs, and relocated complexity derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction refines the contribution from bypassing the 'Euclidean detour' to avoiding global flattening into one Euclidean feature space, explicitly acknowledging log/exp computations. The main claims of strict generalization, second-order representations, six-of-seven MoleculeNet leadership, and depth robustness remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds task-dependent limitations of sign-erasing embeddings, expands the discussion of equivariant applicability, and introduces a flat-versus-non-flat bundle interpretation. EEG conclusions now distinguish within-session competitiveness from cross-session leadership. Appendix I interprets greater perturbation sensitivity as stronger edge dependence while expressly declining to claim superior noise robustness.

D1.justification: Appendix D.4 newly provides a code-repository location, and Appendix E.5 distinguishes rerun EEG baselines from quoted results. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, numerical precision, and software dependencies are retained. The repository's contents or accessibility cannot be verified from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning SPD metrics, neuroimaging, EEG comparison methods, and oversmoothing, including Thanwerdas and Pennec, Ju et al., Kobler et al., and Rusch et al. It also discusses MACE and NequIP when positioning a future equivariant extension. The main related-work survey remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include localized introduction and EEG-result rewrites, additional notation explanations, a limitations subsection, acknowledgements, and new appendix sections. Existing complexity and future-work appendices move from G/H to J/K. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantive scaling, depth-diagnostic, and perturbation tables (Tables 9–11), and expands EEG Table 6 with three comparator columns and revised ranking emphasis. Several retained tables move within the layout. Figures 1–3 retain the same graphics; the substantial display additions are tabular.

improvement.justification: The stronger EEG comparison replaces blanket superiority with appropriately qualified rankings, while explicit sign-loss limitations and code-access information improve transparency. New experiments broaden supporting evidence. However, the gain is limited by sparse protocol and uncertainty reporting, the GCN/GraphSAGE ambiguity, and numerical inconsistencies in the new oversmoothing discussion: Table 10 gives BACE energy 0.002 at depth 64, contrary to the stated threshold below 0.001.
